$description: The UCF block theme's styles for plain elements (body copy, headings, links, captions), as data, so the theme and React hosts read one source. scripts/build-tokens.mjs writes them twice: into dist/theme/theme-json.json as theme.json `styles` (references become --wp--preset--* and --wp--custom--*), and into dist/tokens/elements.css for React hosts (references become --ucf-*). Each element is in theme.json's shape. `{group.slug}` names a token in tokens.json; `{role.name}` names a role, which follows the section it sits in. `css` holds what theme.json can't express (underline thickness, text-wrap, colors on p and li): React hosts get it here, and the theme writes it in its own SCSS. SYNC: the theme's tools/sync-tokens.js checks its theme.json `styles` against the kit.

css.$description: A11Y: a role, so a heading in a Dark section is white, not black on black.

h4.$description: SPEC: h4 to h6 are body type, not display: sentence case, heavier.

:hover.$description: SPEC: hover thickens the underline as well as changing color, so it never relies on hue.

text.$description: Rules for elements theme.json has no entry for. React hosts get them in elements.css; the theme writes its own.

p, li.$description: WHY a role: copy follows the composition it sits in, as headings and links do.
